headline: Bangladesh thumped 3-0 by Malaysia in ASEAN Cup opener
summary: The national team suffered a disappointing start to the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup 2026, struggling to create meaningful chances against the Malaysian side.
details: Bangladesh suffered a heavy 3-0 defeat against Malaysia in their Group A opening match of the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup 2026.
The match took place at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia, where Thomas Dooley's side struggled to find their rhythm.
Malaysia's winger Arif Aiman dominated the first half, netting a brace to put his team in a commanding position.
The lead was further extended in the 52nd minute when forward Bergson scored the third goal for the Malaysian side.
Throughout the game, the Bangladeshi players struggled to create any meaningful scoring opportunities against a disciplined defense.
Bangladesh will now look to bounce back in their next Group A fixture against Singapore on September 28 at the same venue.
caption:
A tough start in Jakarta. 🇧🇩

Bangladesh falls 3-0 to Malaysia in their ASEAN Cup opener.

Bangladesh suffered a heavy 3-0 defeat against Malaysia in their Group A opening match of the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup 2026.

The match took place at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia, where Thomas Dooley's side struggled to find their rhythm.

Malaysia's winger Arif Aiman dominated the first half, netting a brace to put his team in a commanding position.

The lead was further extended in the 52nd minute when forward Bergson scored the third goal for the Malaysian side.

Throughout the game, the Bangladeshi players struggled to create any meaningful scoring opportunities against a disciplined defense.

Bangladesh will now look to bounce back in their next Group A fixture against Singapore on September 28 at the same venue.

caption:
1,084 children have died from measles symptoms since March. Three more lives were lost in just 24 hours.

Three more children died within 24 hours due to measles symptoms, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Friday.

Since March 15, a total of 1,084 children have died from measles or measles-like symptoms across the country.

Of these deaths, 101 cases were confirmed as measles, while 983 deaths were associated with measles symptoms.

Since March 15, 108,833 people have shown symptoms of the disease, with 21,015 cases being confirmed as measles.

Additionally, 164,248 suspected measles patients have been admitted to hospitals since March.

Of those admitted, 157,807 patients have recovered and been discharged from the hospital.
